title: While Loop
description: Hold a button to re-calibrate a light sensor — the code stays in a while loop as long as you press.

steps.clip: You need: an Arduino Uno and its USB cable, a breadboard, 1 × light sensor (photoresistor), 2 × 10 kΩ resistor, 1 × pushbutton, 2 × 220 Ω resistor, 2 × LED, and some jumper wires.
Push the light sensor in, its two legs in two different columns.
hints: It works either way round.
steps.goal: Put the light sensor on the breadboard.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's 5V pin → the red + row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. One leg of the light sensor → that same row.
hints: Either leg works.
steps.goal: Connect one leg of the light sensor to 5V.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the light sensor's other leg to pin A0 on the Arduino.
hints: Pin A0 is on the ANALOG IN side of the Arduino.
steps.goal: Connect the light sensor's other leg to pin A0.

steps.clip: Push a 10 kΩ resistor in: one leg in the same column as the pin A0 wire, the other leg in an empty column.
hints: The light sensor and this resistor share the 5 V between them — so the pin's voltage changes as the light sensor does.
steps.goal: Put a 10 kΩ resistor next to the pin A0 wire.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's GND pin → the blue − row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. That resistor's other leg → that same row.
hints: Now the reading goes up when the light gets brighter.
steps.goal: Connect the 10 kΩ resistor to GND.

steps.clip: Push the button in across the middle gap: two legs above the gap, two below.
hints: The two legs in one column (above and below the gap) are always joined inside the button.
Pressing joins the left column to the right column.
steps.goal: Put the button across the middle gap.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the button's left column (top half) to pin 2 on the Arduino.
hints: Any hole in that column works.
Pin 2 is on the Arduino's row of numbered sockets.
steps.goal: Connect one side of the button to pin 2.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the button's right column (bottom half) to the red + row.
hints: When you press, 5V flows through the button to the pin.
steps.goal: Connect the other side of the button to 5V.

steps.clip: Push a 10 kΩ resistor in: one leg in the button's left column (bottom half), the other leg in an empty column.
hints: This is a pull-down: it keeps the pin LOW until you press.
Without it the pin 'floats' and reads random values.
steps.goal: Put a 10 kΩ resistor on the button's pin 2 side.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the 10 kΩ resistor's other leg to the blue − row.
hints: Now the pin reads LOW, and HIGH only while you press.
steps.goal: Connect the 10 kΩ resistor to GND.

steps.clip: Push a 220 Ω resistor into the breadboard. Put its two legs in two different columns.
hints: A resistor works either way round.
It protects the LED — without it the LED can burn out.
steps.goal: Put the resistor for the LED on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Run a wire from one leg of the resistor you just placed to pin 9 on the Arduino.
hints: Put the wire in any hole in the same column as the leg.
Pin 9 is on the Arduino's row of numbered sockets.

steps.clip: Put the LED in: the long leg in the same column as that resistor's other leg, the short leg in the next column.
hints: The long leg is + (the anode). Backwards, the LED stays dark.
Legs in the same column are connected — no wire needed.
steps.goal: Connect the LED's long leg (+) to the resistor.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the LED's short leg to the blue − row.
hints: The short leg is − (the cathode).
GND is the minus side of the circuit.
steps.goal: Connect the LED's short leg (−) to GND.

steps.clip: Push a 220 Ω resistor into the breadboard. Put its two legs in two different columns.
hints: A resistor works either way round.
It protects the LED — without it the LED can burn out.
steps.goal: Put the resistor for the second LED on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Run a wire from one leg of the resistor you just placed to pin 13 on the Arduino.
hints: Put the wire in any hole in the same column as the leg.
Pin 13 is on the Arduino's row of numbered sockets.

steps.clip: Put the second LED in: the long leg in the same column as that resistor's other leg, the short leg in the next column.
hints: The long leg is + (the anode). Backwards, the LED stays dark.
Legs in the same column are connected — no wire needed.
steps.goal: Connect the second LED's long leg (+) to the resistor.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the second LED's short leg to the blue − row.
hints: The short leg is − (the cathode).
GND is the minus side of the circuit.
steps.goal: Connect the second LED's short leg (−) to GND.

steps.clip: Copy the code into the Arduino IDE and click Upload. Hold the button and cover and uncover the light sensor (the second LED is on while you hold). Let go: the first LED follows the light.
